body:
A narrow candidate fix is ready for this issue: [fork branch](https://github.com/linhongyu510/hono/tree/fix/preserve-multipart-bytes), commit `7020f42f7bffc26985978df6ba3621cd71afd3e7`.

When the first Hono body read is `text()` (including the read inside `json()`) and the media type is multipart, it caches the original `ArrayBuffer` before decoding. Subsequent form parsing, binary reads, and `cloneRawRequest()` therefore use the original bytes. The production change adds eight lines and annotates the recursive private helper.

The regression uploads all byte values `0..255`. Before the fix, parsing after `text()` returns a 512-byte file; after the fix, all 256 bytes match. Tests also cover concurrent reads, a failed JSON parse, repeated parsing, `parseBody()`, cloning with the original Content-Type/Content-Length, and stream failures. A Bun middleware regression uses a generated multipart boundary.

Local validation on Node 24.19.0 and Bun 1.4.0:

- Core + Node suites: 4,187 passed, 37 skipped; Bun suite: 17 passed.
- Type checking, build, and formatting passed; lint has no errors and one existing warning outside the change.
- The same standalone reproduction still fails on #5385 at `cc92a59f` and #5536 at `f7d4c67c`, with both generated and explicit boundaries. It passes on this branch in both runtimes.

The tradeoff is retaining the original buffer for multipart text-first reads; repeated text reads decode from that buffer. This could also be folded into the ongoing cache work in #5385/#5536.

Implementation and local verification were AI-assisted. Sharing the fork branch for maintainer review in accordance with the contribution guide.
